review_notes: Newsom judicial -1/medium (reversed from +1 in the primary) holds on new first-person evidence. His judicial-philosophy page commits to 'impartial application of the law as written, grounded in precedent', says judges apply rather than make policy, and rules out 'agendas, ideologies' [S5]. His pamphlet adds 'not focused on politics and ideology' [S1]. These are pole_a statements. 'Mindful of real-world impacts' [S5] and 'fair, pragmatic, and equitable outcomes' [S1] temper them, which correctly caps the score at -1. A single page means medium, not high. Newsom safety -1/medium survives, but the basis leans on the wrong evidence. The Stranger's account of his January 2025 Burien remark about threatening arrest [S8] is a secondhand report from an outlet endorsing his opponent. It is also an encampment-policy statement, not bail, diversion or formation evidence, so under the judicial safety rule it should not be load-bearing. The score is still correct on formation alone: 34 years of prosecution and city-attorney work with no defense practice [S1][S4]. His diversion language 'while protecting the community' [S1] is the shared, non-differentiating kind the _contest.md lists under 'Not differentiating'. That matches Walls (SW Pos 5), Tse and Rose-Akins at -1/medium. Suggest rewording the basis to rest on formation and dropping 'Moved from 0... on the new Burien evidence'. Newsom experience -1/medium (34 years, pro tem in KCDC and SMC [S1][S7]) and Rothstein experience 0/medium (20 years of practice, pro tem only since 2024 [S3]) are consistent with the primary and with Walls and Rose-Akins. Rothstein safety +2/medium: his bail statement (release should turn on flight risk and danger, 'not whether they have sufficient resources to afford bail' [S3]) was re-verified, and with his drug-court and recovery-board service and 20-year defense formation [S1][S3] it remains the deepest safety evidence in the judicial set. Rothstein judicial +1/medium was tested against the primary NE Pos 1 refutation, which dropped Trasen's judicial score to low because it double-counted her treatment plank. Rothstein's judicial evidence ('the people's court', treatment, second chances [S1]) also overlaps his safety evidence. Here, though, the rubric explicitly routes Seattle Municipal Court judicial placement through bail/diversion posture, and the primary refutation upheld this exact score on that ground. With Newsom now explicitly at -1, the spread reflects a real stated difference, so it stands. No score uses the King County Democrats, The Stranger or the Seattle Times endorsements. Copy flags: (1) Newsom's summary says he is endorsed by 'the retiring incumbent'. Gregory's retirement is asserted only in Newsom's own statement [S1], and the court's profile does not mention it [S13]. The race_blurb handles this correctly ('term ends in January 2027'). Suggest 'endorsed by the Seattle Times and incumbent Judge Willie Gregory'. (2) Rothstein's summary calls him 'the race's most explicit candidate on bail', which reads as comparative and evaluative. The dossier's finding is that he is the only candidate with a documented bail position [S3], and the more neutral wording would be 'and has published a position on bail'. (3) Both sides' highlights cite the primary-era Seattle Times/Stranger endorsements and KCBA status evenly, and the race_blurb is balanced.
